specification: Implement a small recurrence-rule library in the package recur. recur/rule.py defines parse_rule(text); recur/expand.py defines expand(rule, start, end); recur/__init__.py re-exports both names so that `from recur import parse_rule, expand` works. parse_rule(text): text must be a str, otherwise raise TypeError. A rule is a ';'-separated list of KEY=VALUE parts. Keys are case-sensitive and must be one of FREQ, INTERVAL, BYDAY, BYMONTHDAY, COUNT, UNTIL; whitespace is not allowed anywhere. Raise ValueError for: an empty part (this includes empty text, a leading ';' and a trailing ';'), a part with no '=' or with an empty value, an unknown key, a duplicate key, a missing FREQ, a FREQ other than DAILY, WEEKLY or MONTHLY, BYDAY used with a FREQ other than WEEKLY, BYMONTHDAY used with a FREQ other than MONTHLY, and COUNT combined with UNTIL. INTERVAL and COUNT must be positive decimal integers written with ASCII digits only (no sign, no decimal point; leading zeros are allowed), otherwise raise ValueError. BYDAY is a comma-separated list of the codes MO TU WE TH FR SA SU (upper case only). BYMONTHDAY is a comma-separated list whose items are either an integer from 1 to 31 written with ASCII digits, or the literal -1 meaning the last day of the month. An empty list item or any other item is a ValueError. UNTIL must be exactly eight ASCII digits YYYYMMDD naming a real calendar date, otherwise ValueError. parse_rule returns a new dict with exactly these keys: 'freq' (the FREQ string), 'interval' (int, 1 when absent), 'byday' (tuple of ints with 0=Monday ... 6=Sunday, duplicates removed, ascending; empty tuple when absent), 'bymonthday' (tuple of ints, duplicates removed, ascending so that -1 comes first; empty tuple when absent), 'count' (int or None) and 'until' (datetime.date or None). expand(rule, start, end): rule is a dict returned by parse_rule and must not be modified. start and end must be instances of exactly datetime.date (datetime.datetime instances and every other type raise TypeError). Return a new list of datetime.date objects, in ascending order and without duplicates, containing the occurrences d of the rule with start <= d <= end. The series is anchored at start but start is an occurrence only if the rule produces it. DAILY: start, start + interval days, start + 2*interval days, and so on. WEEKLY: weeks run from Monday to Sunday. The first week is the week that contains start; occurrences fall in that week and in every interval-th week after it, on each weekday listed in byday (on the weekday of start when byday is empty). Days of the first week that are earlier than start are not occurrences. MONTHLY: the first month is the calendar month that contains start; occurrences fall in that month and in every interval-th month after it, on each day number listed in bymonthday (on start.day when bymonthday is empty), where -1 means the last day of that particular month. A day number that does not exist in a month (for example 31 in April or 30 in February) yields no occurrence in that month; it is never moved to another day. A date that is listed twice (for example 30 and -1 in a 30-day month) occurs once. Dates earlier than start are not occurrences. UNTIL is inclusive: no occurrence is later than until. COUNT limits the series itself: only the first count occurrences of the series (in ascending order, never counting dates earlier than start) exist, and end then removes those later than end. When start is later than end the result is an empty list. Dates beyond datetime.date.max are never produced; very large intervals therefore simply end the series instead of raising.
